processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Sample heated to 1200 °C at a rate of 10 °C/s.
Homogenized by holding for 120 s at 1200 °C.
Cooled from 1200 °C to the set temperature (1100 °C for this sample) at a rate of 5 °C/s.
Held for 15 s at the set temperature before compression so the temperature difference between inside and outside the sample was the same.

Isothermal constant strain rate compression of the Ø8 mm × 12 mm cylindrical sample to 60% reduction (max true strain 0.92) at 1 s^-1 and 1100 °C. Mica foils with high-temperature lubricant were affixed to the two end faces to reduce friction and deformation non-uniformity. This sample = T 1100 °C, ε̇ 1 s^-1.
After compression the sample was sprayed with water to cool the steel down.

structures.overall_structure: Pre-deformation as-forged microstructure: large polygonal grains delimited by bright etched boundaries, with dark grain interiors containing abundant fine, closely spaced, parallel light-grey striations (segregation banding); the striation direction changes from grain to grain, giving a strongly banded dendritic/interdendritic segregation contrast rather than a uniform solid solution. Chemical heterogeneity present in the as-forged condition.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Large grains relative to the 100 µm scale bar — individual grains span roughly one to a few times the bar length

structures.overall_structure: Microstructure after 60% hot compression at 1100 °C / 1 s^-1, showing non-uniform deformation across three zones (1 difficult deformation, 2 small deformation, 3 large deformation). Degree of dynamic recrystallization increases zone 3 (large) > zone 2 (small) > zone 1 (difficult). With increasing temperature the DRX volume fraction increases and recrystallized grain size grows.

microstructure_list.region: difficult deformation zone (zone 1, near loading surfaces)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Coarse grains with few, long straight boundaries (least recrystallized of the three zones)

microstructure_list.region: small deformation zone (zone 2, ends adjacent to the horizontal centre line)
large deformation zone (zone 3, central band, core of the compressed sample)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Fine, fairly equiaxed recrystallized grain structure; the core (large-deformation zone) is the region from which DRX grain size is measured

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Isothermal constant-strain-rate hot compression to 60% (max true strain 0.92) on Gleeble-3500; hot-deformation (rheological) flow stress measured

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: True stress–true strain (rheological) curve at T = 1100 °C, ε̇ = 1 s^-1: curve peaks near 155 MPa then softens; peak strain ≈ 0.1–0.2 (general value for this steel)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Characteristic values of the rheological stress curve (critical, peak and steady-state strain/stress) as functions of lnZ; for this sample lnZ = 58.68

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Characteristic values obtained from the flow-stress-curve models expressed in terms of lnZ: εc = 0.0093 lnZ − 0.43; σc = 1.0048(lnZ)^2 − 97.23 lnZ + 2379.08; εp = 0.020 lnZ − 0.94; σp = 0.98(lnZ)^2 − 94.21 lnZ + 2291.34; εs = 0.034 lnZ − 1.53; σs = 0.55(lnZ)^2 − 46.96 lnZ + 984.67

characterization_methods.technique: Isothermal constant-strain-rate hot compression testing (thermo-mechanical simulation)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: T = 900–1150 °C (this sample 1100 °C), ε̇ = 0.01–10 s^-1 (this sample 1 s^-1), 60% compression (true strain 0.92)
characterization_methods.purpose: To obtain the rheological (flow) stress curves and study hot deformation / dynamic recrystallization behaviour
characterization_methods.key_findings: Steel is negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive; peak stress at 1100 °C, 1 s^-1 ≈ 155 MPa; DRX activation energy 669.844 kJ/mol

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Compressed sample split in half along the axial axis; prepared, ground, polished and etched; microstructure imaged in the three deformation zones (100 µm scale bars)
characterization_methods.purpose: To observe the microstructure evolution and measure DRX grain size in the deformation zones
characterization_methods.key_findings: Three deformation zones show different DRX degrees (zone 3 > zone 2 > zone 1); DRX grain size increases with temperature and decreasing strain rate

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Etching solution: 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction)
characterization_methods.purpose: To reveal grain boundaries and microstructure before optical imaging

computational_details.simulation_method: Arrhenius hyperbolic-sine constitutive analysis with linear regression of ln ε̇ vs ln[sinh(ασp)] and ln[sinh(ασp)] vs 1000/T
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Fit quality reported via relationship maps (Fig. 4); fitted lines are not parallel, so the calculated Q is an average value over the experimental range

analytical_models.equation_role: Relates strain rate, peak stress and temperature to determine DRX activation energy

parameters.name: k1 (avg slope, ln ε̇ vs ln[sinh(ασp)])

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: lnZ increases with strain rate and decreases with temperature, matching the flow-stress trend

analytical_models.equation_role: Temperature-compensated strain rate characterizing combined effect of T and ε̇ on flow stress
analytical_models.model_note: Full lnZ matrix in Table 1; for ε̇ = 1 s^-1: 68.69, 65.88, 63.29, 60.90, 58.68, 56.62 for 900–1150 °C respectively, giving 58.68 at 1100 °C.

computational_details.simulation_method: Multiple linear/polynomial regression of DRX characteristic values against lnZ; DRX state-diagram construction
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Regression correlation coefficients: σc R = 0.947, εc R = 0.911, σp R = 0.957, εp R = 0.911, σs R = 0.956, εs R = 0.922

analytical_models.equation_role: Express critical, peak and steady-state strain/stress of the flow curve as functions of lnZ
analytical_models.model_note: Used to draw the DRX state diagram (Fig. 7): area A work hardening, area B partial DRX, area C complete DRX

computational_details.simulation_method: Mathematical regression of experimental grain-size data via Levenberg-Marquardt optimization; DEFORM-3D finite element simulation for the hot-compression process
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Billet set as rigid plastic body, die indenter as rigid body; semi-symmetric specimen used to shorten simulation time; contact-interface friction set to shear type with value 0.3; billet-air convection coefficient 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C); simulation matched the thermal-compression experimental conditions
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Correlation analysis and error test of predicted vs experimental grain size: R = 0.996, MRE = 4.53%; absolute error mostly within 3 µm

analytical_models.model_name: DRX average grain size model (eq 11 / eq 12)
analytical_models.equation_role: Predicts DRX average grain size from strain rate and temperature
analytical_models.model_note: Eq 11 form: drex = a·d0^h·ε^p·ε̇^q·exp(Q/RT) + b; initial grain size and strain treated as fixed constants

unmapped_findings: Panel-labelling discrepancy for this sample: the sample is defined as 1100 °C / 1 s^-1 (aliases T=1100 °C, ε̇=1 s^-1, '(e)') and the process snapshot states its microstructure is shown as Fig. 9(e), but the Fig. 9 caption (b0072) labels panel (e) as T = 1050 °C, ε̇ = 1 s^-1, and the figure description (figure_009) states panels (a)–(c) are 1100 °C at 0.01/0.1/10 s^-1 while (d)=950 °C, (e)=1050 °C and (f)=1150 °C at 1 s^-1. There is therefore no Fig. 9 panel explicitly labelled 1100 °C / 1 s^-1; the caption also mislabels the 1150 °C panel as '(d)'. Microstructure content attributed to this sample should be treated with caution.

For this steel, sufficient and relatively fine/uniform DRX grains are obtained by hot working in the ranges 950–1000 °C / 0.01–0.1 s^-1 and 1050–1100 °C / 1–10 s^-1 (b0012, b0065, b0086); the sample at 1100 °C / 1 s^-1 lies within the recommended second range.
Steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material: rheological stress decreases with decreasing strain rate or increasing temperature (b0021, b0024, b0084).

At ε̇ = 0.01 s^-1 the peak stress decreased from 305.4 MPa at 900 °C to 53.8 MPa at 1150 °C (82% reduction); at 10 s^-1 the peak stress decreased by 73% over the same temperature range (b0024) — these are other-condition values, not this sample's.

At 1150 °C and 0.01 s^-1 the DRX grain size exceeds 70 µm (coarse-grain regime), whereas at low T (900–950 °C) and high ε̇ (1–10 s^-1) the DRX grains are small but DRX is insufficient with large remnant original grains (b0063) — provided for context, not for this sample's condition.
The prediction model for DRX average grain size has a high accuracy: R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53% (b0012, b0076–b0080, figure_011).
